correctness.rationale: The cyclic-word-to-closed-walk transfer identity is exact even for k>n because the all-zero periodic word admits no closed walk. The negative transition has order k+1 and nontrivial (k+1)th roots as eigenvalues. Reducing all transition signs mod2 establishes common parity, and the upper-triangular rank-one reflection product yields k-2j at every resonance. The explicit zero and unit/two witnesses prove both directions and exact gaps. Standalone exact-integer checking independently confirms 140 complete Walsh parameter pairs and transfer identities for k<=23; finite checks do not replace the all-parameter argument.

originality.rationale: The new statement covers all integers n,k and determines zero existence and the smallest positive Walsh magnitude, with explicit resonance patterns. The 2009 cycle-domination paper concerns k=3 unsigned enumeration; the 2013 generalized-Fibonacci paper concerns linear-string Gray codes and counting. A previous k=2 cycle-independent-set Fourier classification covers only a strict special case. published-finding corpus searches of run-avoidance, cyclic-window Fourier zeros, domination transforms, and phase/transfer aliases found no implication of the all-k theorem. Negative search is not proof of originality, and a possible older signed-transfer identity remains a bounded risk.
residual_risks: A historical paper on signed cyclic transfer matrices or generalized Lucas functions may contain an equivalent all-k zero/gap statement.

value.rationale: The exact convolution-invertibility and spectral-gap classification of all cyclic window hitting sets is a natural complete invariant across two unbounded parameters. It explains a structural separation between every odd forbidden run length (always invertible, including arbitrary cycle-power dominating sets) and even run lengths (a precise divisibility singularity), with a signed reflection mechanism giving sharp gaps. This goes beyond a single finite case or a routine numerical increment of k=2.
